blocks.text: On Sabbath the following prayer is recited before אשרי
uncertainties: The rubric is in English italics, with unpointed Hebrew אשרי at its end. It is identical to the rubric on s191. It is a Shabbat-only direction, so both Yekum Purkan prayers and the Mi Sheberakh that follow belong to that Shabbat condition. The page states no other condition.

blocks.text: יְקוּם פּוּרְקָן מִן־שְׁמַיָּא חִנָּא וְחִסְדָּא וְרַחֲמֵי וְחַיֵּי אֲרִיכֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי רְוִיחֵי וְסִיַּעְתָּא דִשְׁמַיָּא וּבַרְיוּת גּוּפָא וּנְהוֹרָא מַעַלְיָא: זַרְעָא חַיָּא וְקַיָּמָא זַרְעָא דִּי לָא־יִפְסוּק וְדִי לָא־יִבְטוּל מִפִּתְגָּמֵי אוֹרַיְתָא: לְמָרָנָן וְרַבָּנָן חֲבוּרָתָא קַדִּישָׁתָא. דִּי בְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְדִי בְבָבֶל. לְרֵישֵׁי כַלֵּי וּלְרֵישֵׁי גַלְוָתָא וּלְרֵישֵׁי מְתִיבָתָא וּלְדַיָּנֵי דִי בָבָא: לְכָל־תַּלְמִידֵיהוֹן וּלְכָל־תַּלְמִידֵי תַלְמִידֵיהוֹן וּלְכָל מָן־דְּעָסְקִין בְּאוֹרַיְתָא. מַלְכָּא דְעָלְמָא יְבָרֵךְ יָתְהוֹן יַפִּישׁ חַיֵּיהוֹן וְיַסְגֵּא יוֹמֵיהוֹן וְיִתֵּן אַרְכָה לִשְׁנֵיהוֹן. וְיִתְפָּרְקוּן וְיִשְׁתֵּזְבוּן מִן כָּל־עָקָא וּמִן כָּל־מַרְעִין בִּישִׁין מָרָן דִּי בִשְׁמַיָּא יְהֵא בְּסַעְדְּהוֹן כָּל־זְמַן וְעִדָּן וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן:
uncertainties: פּוּרְקָן is spelled plene, with a shuruq vav. יִבְטוּל is also plene.
The first word of line 6 is כַּלֵּי or כַלֵּי. I can't tell from the image whether its initial kaf has a dagesh.
In בְאַרְעָא and בְבָבֶל I can't tell whether the first bet has a dagesh. I read both as having none.
There is a maqaf after מָן at the end of line 7, and the text continues דְּעָסְקִין on the next line.
No period or colon is printed between בִּישִׁין and מָרָן in this first prayer. The second prayer has a period there.
I could not reliably detect any meteg marks at this resolution. Faint vertical strokes may be present.
Punctuation is printed as shown: colons after מַעַלְיָא, אוֹרַיְתָא and בָבָא, and periods after קַדִּישָׁתָא, בְבָבֶל, בְּאוֹרַיְתָא and לִשְׁנֵיהוֹן.

blocks.text: יְקוּם פּוּרְקָן מִן־שְׁמַיָּא חִנָּא וְחִסְדָּא וְרַחֲמֵי וְחַיֵּי אֲרִיכֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי רְוִיחֵי וְסִיַּעְתָּא דִשְׁמַיָּא וּבַרְיוּת גּוּפָא וּנְהוֹרָא מַעַלְיָא זַרְעָא חַיָּא וְקַיָּמָא זַרְעָא דִּי לָא־יִפְסוּק וְדִי לָא־יִבְטוּל מִפִּתְגָּמֵי אוֹרַיְתָא: לְכָל־קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא הָדֵין. רַבְרְבַיָּא עִם זְעֵרַיָּא טַפְלָא וּנְשַׁיָּא. מַלְכָּא דְעָלְמָא יְבָרֵךְ יָתְכוֹן יַפִּישׁ חַיֵּיכוֹן וְיַסְגֵּא יוֹמֵיכוֹן וְיִתֵּן אַרְכָה לִשְׁנֵיכוֹן. וְתִתְפָּרְקוּן וְתִשְׁתֵּזְבוּן מִן כָּל־עָקָא וּמִן כָּל־מַרְעִין בִּישִׁין. מָרָן דִּי בִשְׁמַיָּא יְהֵא בְּסַעְדְּכוֹן. כָּל־זְמַן וְעִדָּן. וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן:
uncertainties: Unlike the first prayer, no colon is printed after מַעַלְיָא here.
The line ends after לָא־, and the text continues יִבְטוּל on the next line.
The periods after בִּישִׁין, בְּסַעְדְּכוֹן and וְעִדָּן are printed as transcribed.
I can't tell whether the first letter of בִשְׁמַיָּא has a dagesh. I read it as having none.

blocks.text: מִי שֶׁבֵּרַךְ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, הוּא יְבָרֵךְ אֶת־כָּל־הַקָּהָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה, עִם כָּל־קְהִלּוֹת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, הֵם וּנְשֵׁיהֶם וּבְנֵיהֶם
uncertainties: This is set in a larger typeface and continues onto the next page. The last word on this page is וּבְנֵיהֶם.
The mark after הַזֶּה at the line end looks like a comma, but it is slightly unclear.

blocks.text: 85 Morning Prayer for the New Year 85
On Sabbath the following prayer is recited before אשרי
uncertainties: אשרי is unpointed Hebrew inside the English rubric.

blocks.text: Let there arise salvation from heaven, mercy and kindness, compassion, long life, abundant sustenance, divine help, bodily health, heavenly enlightenment, living and enduring seed who do not interrupt or abandon study of the words of the Torah, to the masters and teachers, the holy congregations in the Land of Israel and in Babylon, the heads of the learned gathering, the Exilarchs, the heads of the academies and the judges at the gate, to all their pupils and all the pupils of their pupils and all who occupy themselves with the Law. May the King of the world bless them, prolong their lives, increase their days and give length to their years. May they be saved and delivered from every need and all evil happenings. May our Lord in Heaven aid them at every time and season, and let us say: Amen.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates "en-during" across a line break. It is joined here.

blocks.text: Let there arise salvation from heaven, mercy and kindness, long life, abundant food, divine help, bodily health, heavenly enlightenment, living and enduring seed, who do not interrupt or abandon study of the words of the Torah, to this holy congregation, old and young, children and women. May the King of the world bless you, prolong your life, increase your days and give length to your years. May you be saved and delivered from every need and all evil happenings. May our Lord in heaven aid you at every time and season, and let us say: Amen.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates "happen-ings" across a line break. It is joined here.
"heaven" is lowercase in this paragraph, while the first paragraph has "Heaven".

blocks.text: He who blessed our fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, bless all this holy congregation together with all other holy congregations; them, their wives, sons and daughters
uncertainties: The text continues onto the next page.

No cantillation accents are visible on s190; this is prayer text in Aramaic and Hebrew with vowel points only. I could not reliably detect meteg marks at the available resolution.
The Hebrew on s190 has two sizes: the Yekum Purkan prayers are in regular type and the Mi Sheberakh is in larger type. The bottom quarter of both pages is blank.
